title: Identification and characterization of antimicrobial antibodies in the serum of patients with periodontitis
summary: The aim of this study is basic research into new therapeutic approaches for periodontitis. It is assumed that the immune system in periodontitis patients has produced protective substances known as antibodies, which are intended to contain the infection. Ideally, an antibody can be extracted from the blood of periodontitis patients, serving as the foundation for a new medication that could benefit many people. Antibodies are components of the human immune system designed to defend against infections and are capable of combating pathogens. When an infection occurs, the human immune system generates various antibodies. Thanks to new biotechnological methods, we are now able to systematically search for these antibodies and produce them artificially. This not only aids in understanding infectious diseases and their interactions with our immune system but also facilitates the development of new therapeutic approaches.

interventions.name: Participants who have been afflicted with periodontitis for several years and/or have an especially progressive form of the condition (Grade C). To establish a control group, approximately 10% of the participants should not exhibit any periodontitis-related illness.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The following general criteria must be met for inclusion in the study:

- Capacity to provide informed consent
- Patients with periodontitis as well as individuals without a diagnosis of periodontitis, provided all other inclusion criteria are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

Additionally, the following criteria must be checked and satisfied immediately before blood collection:

- Puncture site: Free from lesions or infections
- Presence of a signed informed consent form for participation in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- Existing cytopenias (leukocytes <1,500/μl, platelets <50,000/μl, or hemoglobin <12 g/dl)
- Cardiac complications (e.g., pulmonary arterial hypertension).
- Presence of infectious diseases.
- No blood sample collection for B-cell isolation in individuals with a body weight <50 kg
- Blood donation or significant blood loss (e.g., surgery) within the last 8 weeks (men) or 12 weeks (women).
- Blood pressure: systolic: 100–180 mm Hg, diastolic: below 100 mm Hg.
- Pulse: within the normal range, frequency 50–110/min; potential donors engaged in intense sports activities with a pulse rate below 50/min may be considered.
- Within one week after minor surgery (e.g., biopsy, tooth extraction, etc.), or 2 or 3 months (as mentioned above) after major surgery (e.g., involving the opening of the chest cavity or abdominal cavity) or any other surgery with an increased risk of post-operative bleeding
- Any deterioration in the general health status, e.g., weight loss >2 kg, diabetic metabolic state, pulmonary exacerbation, or loss of lung function (FEV1 > 10%) in the past 3 months
- No fever
